request.spec:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people list now has a sort select (`data-testid="sort-by"`) with the options added, name, grade and due-total. `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec.

How it works:
- **Front end only.** I didn't change the server or the stored data, so positions, rollups, audit records and every action that uses list order behave exactly as before.
- **Per user's screen.** The choice is kept in the URL (`?sort=`), the same way "show retired" is. So it stays put when you re-load a sheet, and another user's screen starts at "added".
- **name** compares names the way the server does: trimmed and lower-cased, so `ada` comes before `Ben`.
- **grade** sorts by the grade in force on the sheet's today.
- **due-total** sorts lowest first, using the same capped figure the row shows (it comes from `useSheetTotals`), with n/a last. That means it reorders when a hold or the cap changes.
- **Ties** keep list order.

The changes are a new file, `src/main/frontend/features/people/SortBy.tsx`, and a few lines in `src/main/frontend/features/people/people.slot.tsx` that sort the rows on screen and place the select next to "show retired".
